title: Sourcing workflow: MSA/DPA & SLA finalization huddle
summary: Kickoff to finalize MSA/DPA redlines and agree SLA thresholds for pilot. Procurement focused on pricing lane, legal on data handling and DPA exceptions, infra on VPC/KMS and latency SLAs. Agreed next steps: share redlines, security pack, pilot SLO sheet and schedule benchmarking window.
topics: DPA clauses: data residency and subprocessing
SLA thresholds: p99 latency, uptime, rollback
KMS / keying options and egress costs
action_items: Jordan Martinez - Send MSA redlines + consolidated comment spreadsheet - 2025-05-07
Priya Shah - Share detailed security pack (SOC2, ISO attestation, audit logs) - 2025-05-06
Liam O'Connor - Schedule 4-hour benchmarking window and provide test harness instructions - 2025-05-09
Sophie Li - Confirm procurement gating date and signoff committee members - 2025-05-12
Daniel Reyes - Return DPA exception list and preferred language for subprocessor clause - 2025-05-08
next_steps: AE to circulate redlines and pricing lanes
SE to provide security docs and pilot SLO worksheet
Customer to confirm pilot dates and test data residency needs
meeting_header: Date: 2025-05-02 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Jordan M., Priya S., Liam O., Sophie L., Daniel R., Avery B.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Martinez: Alright, thanks everyone for joining. we're on the 15:00 UTC slot, thanks for shifting. quick agenda: final MSA/DPA redlines, SLA thresholds for the pilot, and next steps for procurement/legal.
[00:22] Sophie Li: yep, thanks. we just want to make sure the DPA has clear residency language — some of our records must stay in-region, and we need KMS options that support customer-managed keys.
[00:35] Priya Shah: understood, Sophie. Redwood supports both platform KMS and customer KMS bring-your-own-key; there are documented flows for key rotation and HSM integration. we'll send the tech note.
[01:03] Daniel Reyes: hi, quick one — can you clarify subprocessor list? previous vendor templates required explicit subprocessor disclosure, and our legal team wants that in the DPA.
[01:15] Liam O'Connor: yes, we maintain a subprocessor registry, but the transcribed docs sometimes show it as "sub processer" in older exports, sorry for any confusion. we'll include current registry link and a commit clause for notice windows.
[02:10] Jordan Martinez: on SLAs, procurement is looking for a p99 latency target and uptime numbers for the dedicated tier vs hosted. Sophie, what's your procurement target?
[02:22] Sophie Li: Ideally p95 < 150ms for chat endpoints, p99 under 400ms, and uptime 99.9 for production. we understand tradeoffs with cost.
[02:40] Priya Shah: those are tight for some model+sequence length combos — especially for long context. we can propose canary rollout with a baseline model variant, and then dedicated capacity. Redwood Dedicate — sorry, Redwood Dedicated — offers the SLA backing.
[03:18] Avery Brooks: one more infra note: we need private deployment (VPC) connectivity with strict egress rules. also, egress billing model matters for our FinOps.
[03:35] Jordan Martinez: yes, we'll outline the egress fee tiers. important to note we offer routing policies so requests can remain in-region.
[04:05] Daniel Reyes: on the MSA, we have a couple of non-standard asks: indemnity cap alignment and a more stringent data retention clause. i'll send redlines, but can you flag which items are usually negotiated vs hard no?
[04:18] Priya Shah: absolutely. typically data retention windows are adjustable, indemnity cap is negotiable within standard enterprise ranges; anything involving source code or model IP is trickier.
[05:00] Sophie Li: also need to know about audit rights. our compliance team requires quarterly attestation and the ability to request audit artifacts.
[05:13] Liam O'Connor: we can provide SOC2 reports and ISO attestation, and we instrument audit logs per token and route — redwood console has token-level traces.
[06:20] Jordan Martinez: let's walk through a proposed pilot acceptance checklist: 1) latency/throughput benchmarks, 2) data residency validation, 3) DPA signed, 4) smoke tests for model outputs, 5) billing and egress confirmation. any additions?
[06:38] Avery Brooks: add KMS key rotation validation and RBAC for service accounts.
[06:52] Priya Shah: noted. i'll include those in the SLO sheet.
[08:10] Sophie Li: pricing question — procurement prefers committed monthly blocks for predictability, but we need clarity on burst handling and overage rates. how do you typically price that?
[08:25] Jordan Martinez: we have reserved capacity (Dedicated) for predictable throughput and burst capacity at pre-agreed tiers. pricing model: reserved commit + overage per token / embedding. we'll provide an example cost model tied to the pilot usage.
[09:02] Daniel Reyes: will there be a separate contract for Dedicated? or is it an attachment to the MSA?
[09:11] Jordan Martinez: generally it's a SOW or capacity attachment under the MSA. we'll show a sample SOW.
[11:00] [speaker overlap, crosstalk]
[11:05] Priya Shah: technical deep dive — for benchmarking: provide 10k sample requests with distribution of sequence lengths and concurrency targets. we'll run tests against both hosted and a Dedicated pool in a staging region. note: KV cache warmup can impact first-run latency so we document warm vs steady state.
[11:37] Avery Brooks: our data set includes many long docs, so KV caching and prefix caching behavior matters. also, can you quantify cold start times when scaling up?
[11:50] Liam O'Connor: cold starts depend on model size and GPU availability; with our autoscaler cold starts usually in 30-120s range for large weights, but we have burst capacity options to reduce that. we'll surface exact metrics in the benchmarking notes.
[13:12] Sophie Li: further on DPA, the subprocessing clause — do you allow a 30-day notice for adding subprocessors? that's our preferred window.
[13:25] Jordan Martinez: yes, typical notice windows are 30 days; we'll capture that in the DPA draft.
[14:03] Daniel Reyes: something to watch: encryption in transit and at rest must be AES-256 and modern TLS; also key custody options for regulatory review.
[14:20] Priya Shah: we use TLS 1.2+ and AES-256 at rest. customer-managed keys can be integrated via KMS.
[15:38] Jordan Martinez: procurement asked about term length and early termination for convenience — any hard constraints?
[15:50] Sophie Li: we prefer a 12-month pilot commitment with exit on 30 days for non-viability, but pricing committee may want different lock-ins.
[16:05] Jordan Martinez: we can model a 3-month pilot followed by a 12-month committed period; we'll quote both.
[17:45] [audio artifact: "uh" and muffled speech]
[18:00] Liam O'Connor: regarding logs and PII, we can redact user-submitted PII at ingress if you need, but that affects usefulness of eval logs. we'll document masking strategies.
[18:30] Daniel Reyes: masking is fine, but audit trail must reflect masking operations.
[20:02] Sophie Li: for procurement, the final approvals depend on legal signoff and FinOps review; our committee meets bi-weekly. next meeting on 2025-05-12.
[20:20] Jordan Martinez: ok, i'll target sending the consolidated docs before that date so you can circulate.
[22:45] Priya Shah: small note on model fallback and graceful degradation — we support automatic fallback to smaller variants when Dedicated capacity is constrained, and we can document how routing policies affect cost and latency.
[23:03] Avery Brooks: can we get a simple matrix: model variant, expected p95/p99, cost multiplier? that would help FinOps.
[23:15] Liam O'Connor: yes — we'll create a model economics sheet.
[25:00] Sophie Li: on the DPA we might need data residency clause to specify EU only for certain datasets — do you support EU-only hosting?
[25:12] Jordan Martinez: yes, we have region-specific routing and can pin requests to EU regions. for private deployments we can do on-prem or VPC with customer control.
[27:40] Daniel Reyes: redlines process — i'll return a collated DPA with comments inline; Jordan, would you prefer track changes or a comment spreadsheet?
[27:52] Jordan Martinez: a comment spreadsheet is easiest for procurement to route; we can take tracked changes for the legal team if needed.
[29:10] [short pause]
[29:30] Priya Shah: pilot checklist recap — we'll prepare a one-pager: bench steps, data residency validation, KMS test, RBAC checks, SLO targets.
[30:05] Sophie Li: perfect. also include a billing example for committed vs burst scenarios; for our approval committee that's critical.
[31:20] Jordan Martinez: action owner recap we'll put into the email: MSA redlines, security pack, benchmark window, pricing example, and pilot SLO worksheet.
[32:45] Daniel Reyes: can you confirm backup and data deletion guarantees? we need deletion within 30 days on contract termination for certain data classes.
[32:58] Priya Shah: we support configurable retention policies; 30-day deletion is standard for ephemeral logs, for persistent telemetry we can align per DPA.
[34:12] Sophie Li: competition question — have you worked with Anthropic? curious how your SLA and pricing compare.
[34:26] Jordan Martinez: we have benchmarked against Anthropic and others in public docs; main differentiator we highlight is unified serving across hosted, dedicated and private with clear observability. cost profiles vary by workload.
[36:00] [brief laughter] Sophie Li: ok noted.
[36:30] Liam O'Connor: one technical callout: prefix caching and kv cache behaviors can create big token savings for repetitive clinical prompts; we'll provide caching guidance to maximize cost reduction.
[37:10] Avery Brooks: that's helpful — FinOps needs to see delta numbers.
[38:40] Jordan Martinez: timeline: we'll aim to have redlines and docs out by EOD 2025-05-07, security pack by 05-06, benchmarking window planned for second week of May. follow-up readout 2025-05-13. does that work?
[39:01] Sophie Li: yes.
[40:20] Daniel Reyes: two small DPA asks: delete-after-request and audit frequencies — we'll capture those in the exception list.
[40:35] Priya Shah: noted.
[42:00] [speaker 1 labeled as "Speaker 1" due to transcription error] Speaker 1: um one more note on SLA credits — do you offer service credits or only termination remedies?
[42:12] Jordan Martinez: we typically offer service credits for measurable SLA misses, and termination remedies for persistent breaches. we'll include proposed credit schedule.
[44:05] Sophie Li: procurement wants to see a cap on cumulative credits and a runbook for escalations.
[44:20] Liam O'Connor: we'll add an escalation path with on-call contacts and an SLT escalation ladder in the SOW.
[46:05] Jordan Martinez: anything else before we close?
[46:12] Sophie Li: just confirm the readout call time and we'll try to have committee members there.
[46:25] Jordan Martinez: follow-up readout 2025-05-13 10:00 PT, i'll send invite.
[47:00] Daniel Reyes: thanks everyone.
[47:10] Avery Brooks: thanks all.
[47:20] Priya Shah: thanks, bye.
[47:30] Jordan Martinez: bye everyone, talk soon.
[54:00] [meeting end]
